mappings._doc_justification:
NetSuite stores billing addresses as a structured sublist (addressbookList → addressbook → addressLine1, city, state, zip, country). For the calibration sample we flatten the four most common parts (line 1, city, state, zip) into the source schema as separate fields. The migration target — Rootstock Customer__c.Billing_Address__c — is a single TextArea-style field per Rootstock Object Reference for the calibration sample. The four source fields concatenate with comma-space separators per US-postal convention:

  '123 Main St, San Francisco, CA, 94102'

The AI's job: recognize this as a many-to-one mapping (concat_*), pick all four contributing source fields, and produce a sensible separator. The 'right' answer at the field-pair level is a single (billaddr1 → Billing_Address__c) entry with combination_type='concat_comma' and the other three named as contributors.
_doc_citations: NetSuite SuiteScript Records Browser — Customer addressbookList sublist (addressLine1, city, state, zip)
Rootstock Object Reference — Customer__c.Billing_Address__c (per Kaan's calibration — see notes for alternative interpretations)

gold.notes:
Difficulty: HARD. Three orthogonal judgment calls compound here:

  1. Many-to-one collapse vs structured target: Rootstock might NOT use a single Billing_Address__c TextArea. If Rootstock customer addresses live on a related Account record using Salesforce's compound BillingAddress (BillingStreet/BillingCity/BillingState/BillingPostalCode), the gold answer flips to a one-to-one-per-component mapping (4 separate (source → target) tuples), NOT a concat. This is the most likely place for the AI to be 'right' but Claude to be 'wrong' relative to actual Rootstock convention.

  2. Separator format: comma-space ('123 Main, City, ST, 90000') vs newline ('123 Main\nCity, ST 90000') vs no-separator. The Postal Service convention is two-line; the SF in-app display convention varies by org. Picked comma-space for the gold; flag for Kaan.

  3. country handling: omitted from the source schema for the calibration sample (most US-only migrations don't use it); a real customer dataset has billcountry too.

CALIBRATION VALUE: this example is the litmus test for whether Claude's 'obvious vs judgment-call' boundary aligns with Kaan's. If Kaan says 'no, Rootstock customer addresses always go to the related Account.BillingAddress compound field — this gold mapping is wrong', that's the most informative single calibration signal in the whole sample.
